answer: An agent economy resists sybils by issuing identities only at scarce physical booths. A registrar checks an ID and a live photo, issues a private key—a quill—and posts the face hash as a public signal; the ledger rejects a duplicate hash, so one human cannot claim two accounts. Each booth sits on a public mesa, so each extra identity costs one extra human trip. Trust rests on the registrar's duplicate check; a bribed registrar or a person with two faces is the hole. Linear cost deters cheap minting, not a funder who pays many real people if per-identity reward exceeds travel.
